description: CircuitSetupAck signing payload: binds routeId, routeCommitmentDigestHex, hopIndex, relay X25519 pubkey, initiator X25519 pubkey, ackNonce, ackTimestamp, ackExpiry into a canonical CBOR map prefixed by the SHARENET/CIRCUIT/ACK/1 domain tag. Per R-008H: the ack cryptographically binds the relay to the EXACT committed route (routeCommitmentDigest), preventing route substitution. The payload is signed by the relay's Ed25519 key as proof-of-possession + transcript binding.

constants.bodyEncoding: canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 §4.2.2), integer-keyed map per ADR-0004

vectors.name: valid-ack-payload
vectors.description: Call circuitAckSigningPayload with fixed parameters. Capture the exact hex output. This payload is signed by the relay's Ed25519 key as the proof-of-possession + transcript binding (the signature itself is NOT computed in this vector — the payload hex is the artifact under test).

vectors.name: tampered-routeId
vectors.description: Change routeId to a different value. The signing payload hex differs because the CBOR map slot 1 encodes a different text string. A relay signature computed over the original routeId will NOT verify against the tampered payload — this is the route-substitution defense.

input.mutation: routeId changed to a different 32-byte hex string

expected.result: ok (still valid CBOR, but different bytes)

notes: Per R-008H: the ack binds to BOTH the routeId (identity) AND the routeCommitmentDigest (cryptographic binding to the exact committed route). A relay that signs an ack is committing to forward traffic for THIS exact route — substitution of the underlying route (different hops, different terms) is cryptographically detectable. The ack freshness bounds (ackMaxAgeSeconds=120, ackMaxClockSkewSeconds=60) are enforced by processCircuitSetupAck independently of this payload encoding.
